comparison: Perfect alignment with 100% claim overlap (C60-C74). Both evaluations support the detailed characterization of task-irrelevant networks across datasets. OpenEval provides detailed physiological interpretations while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through overall positive assessment.

Perfect alignment with 100% claim overlap (C91-C99). Both evaluations support the characterization of task-synergistic networks and parallel processing findings. OpenEval provides detailed analysis while peer reviewers accept these as part of the framework's demonstration.

Strong alignment with 93.3% claim overlap (C76-C89). Both evaluations support the comprehensive characterization of task-redundant networks. OpenEval provides detailed functional interpretations while peer reviewers accept the specific network structures as demonstrating the framework's capabilities.

Strong alignment with 66.7% claim overlap (C8-C10, C100-C105). Both evaluations support the generalizability findings and cross-validation results. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation while peer reviewers acknowledge successful demonstration across datasets.

Strong alignment with 57.1% claim overlap (C56-C59). Both evaluations support the clinical utility demonstration for stroke prediction. OpenEval highlights single-trial methodology while peer reviewers accept practical applications, though note future validation needed.

Moderate alignment with 46.2% claim overlap (C3, C5-C7, C25, C32). Both evaluations strongly support the methodological innovation of including task parameters in synergy extraction. All reviewers recognize this as a novel and important contribution addressing recognized gaps.

Moderate alignment with 31.2% claim overlap (C119-C123). Both evaluations support claims about improved specificity and alignment with current understanding. OpenEval emphasizes conceptual contribution while peer reviewers acknowledge advancement of motor control understanding.

Partial alignment with 28.6% claim overlap (C52-C53). Both evaluations support the simple gait example demonstrating functional interpretability. OpenEval also includes clinical prediction claims (C56-C59) not addressed in this peer result.

Moderate alignment with 26.7% claim overlap (C20-C21, C23-C24). Both evaluations support claims about limitations of current methods. OpenEval provides extensive background citations while peer reviewers acknowledge the recognized gap in task-based approaches.

Partial alignment with 25% claim overlap (C130, C134-C136). Both evaluations support functional interpretations and task-relevant couplings. OpenEval emphasizes unifying existing approaches while peer reviewers focus on task-based understanding significance.

Partial alignment with 21.4% claim overlap (C129, C132-C133). Both evaluations support specific motor features and novel observations. OpenEval emphasizes capture of known features plus novel findings while peer reviewers describe results as compelling and scientifically sound.

Agreement on uncertainty with 20% claim overlap (C139). Both evaluations rate speculative future application claims as uncertain. OpenEval notes claims are appropriately framed as possibilities while peer reviewers state added value needs more documentation.

Divergence with 18.8% claim overlap (C115-C117). OpenEval supports the conceptual distinction claims, but peer reviewers express uncertainty about whether methods lead to physiologically-based synergies or merely descriptive ML frameworks. This represents a key area of disagreement about interpretation.

Partial alignment with 13.3% claim overlap (C38-C39). Both evaluations support the tripartite classification of muscle interactions. OpenEval emphasizes methodological pipeline while peer reviewers acknowledge this as a key conceptual contribution.

OpenEval supports methodological comparison claims (C107-C108) showing poor CP performance and superior sNM3F performance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific methodological comparison.

OpenEval supports methodological details including percolation analysis validation, community detection rationale, and cross-validation procedures (C51, C143-C144, C154-C157, C159, C162-C163, C166-C167). No corresponding detailed peer review evaluation of these specific methodological choices.
OpenEval supports dataset descriptions and processing methods (C168-C173, C175-C176) as factual descriptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing dataset characterization.

Peer reviewers support the unifying contribution and broad interest to the field (C13, C109, C128, C142). While OpenEval addresses some of these claims in R8 and R10, this specific grouping emphasizing the integrative nature is unique to peer review.
